perf.summary: DtStraightPathOptions lacks an explicit underlying type, defaulting to int while every sibling flags enum in this file is explicitly typed (uint or byte).
perf.currentCost: Enum implicitly backed by System.Int32 (4 bytes). Inconsistent with DtStraightPathFlags (: byte), DtStatus/DtFindPathOptions/DtRaycastOptions (: uint) and DtDetailTriEdgeFlags (: byte) in the same file.
perf.proposedChange: Declare 'public enum DtStraightPathOptions : byte' (values are 0x01/0x02/0x04, all fit in a byte) to match the codebase convention for small flag enums. If ABI/interop with native Detour expects a wider type, use ': uint' instead to match the other Dt* flag enums.
perf.rationale: Consistency makes the intended storage width explicit and avoids accidental signed-vs-unsigned semantics on bit operations. It is currently passed only as a method argument (DtNavMeshQuery), never stored in a blittable struct, so this is API hygiene, not a layout win.
perf.risk: None observable for the bit-test usages (& / != 0) found in DtNavMeshQuery. Only matters if the type is ever marshalled to native code with a fixed-width expectation; pick the width (byte vs uint) that matches that ABI. No behavior change for the current managed callers.

perf.summary: Detail flags (WrongMagic..AlreadyOccupied) use signed int literals (1 << n) inside a uint-backed [Flags] enum, mixing signed and unsigned literal forms.
perf.currentCost: Mixed literal styles: high bits use '1u << 31', detail bits use '1 << 0'. The signed literals are implicitly converted to uint at compile time; correct today but stylistically inconsistent and a latent hazard if a future flag uses bit 31 with the signed form.
perf.proposedChange: Write all flag values with unsigned literals: 1u << 0, 1u << 1, ... 1u << 7, matching the Failure/Success/InProgress entries and the enum's ': uint' base.
perf.rationale: Uniform unsigned literals eliminate any implicit signed->unsigned narrowing and make the all-uint intent explicit, reducing the chance of a sign-extension surprise on a future high-bit flag.
perf.risk: Zero behavior change for the current values (all in bits 0-7, identical numerically). Pure source-level consistency fix.
